newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle futures close mixed, feeders off.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle futures close mixed, feeders off.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mixed, with nearbys pressured by evening of positions and position rolling ahead of the weekend.
Feeder cattle slipped to lower closes on expectations of continued strength in corn futures, traders said.
Live cattle finished 0.300 cent per lb lower to 0.075 higher with August off most at 67.525 cents. Feeder cattle ended off 0.100 to 0.725 with August off the least at 81.525.

Position squaring ahead of the weekend and rolling of long positions into back months weighed on August live cattle in generally slow trade. The market was awaiting the next move in the cash cattle market after prices in that sector rose about $1.00 per cwt this week, traders said.
Although many traders expect cash cattle to gain another $1.00 to $67.00 next week, others expect the cash beef market to top and packer demand to wane soon.

Part of the light trade was attributed to the August option expiration. There was a large open interest in August options and the lower close in futures greatly reduced the potential for options to be exercised, they added.
ABN Amro-Chicogo Corp and Rosenthal Collins sold August futures late while Dean Witter bought, traders said.
In options, locals sold August 86 calls late. Light commission house selling of October calls and February puts was also noted.
